conclusion: Packaging control (the dormant build, LKAI_E15_A unset), status no-change. Warm REPORT Duration paired by (round, request) on CPU part 0xd40: -0.69% mean over 9 rounds (8 below 0, range -2.18 to +0.13%; sign-flip p=0.02734; control split-half noise at most 1.042%), verdict no-change. The pre-declared verdict rule (E13's): faster only if every round is below 0, the sign-flip p < 0.05 and the mean exceeds the control's split-half noise; otherwise no-change. Median 613 vs 608 ms. Answers: 1440/1440 bit-identical to ctl for the same request and CPU part, and 1344/1344 bit-identical to P1's reference (96 answers on parts the reference lacks). Cold first request +0.099 s, 95% CI [-0.067, +0.186] (n=[43, 45]); restored first request -0.012 s [-0.115, +0.047] (n=[26, 26]). Loaded variants: 0xd0c: armv8.0_1,armv8.2_2 (unchanged); 0xd40: armv8.0_1,armv8.6_1 (changed); 0xd4f: armv8.0_1,armv8.6_2 (changed). Other CPU parts: 0xd0c: +0.5% over 5 round(s) (1 below 0, 4 above), underpowered; 0xd4f: -0.1% over 4 round(s) (2 below 0, 2 above), underpowered. Errors: 0 function, 0 client-transport; restore ReadTimeout rows 0. Warm arms interleaved pass by pass within each round; cold and restore are sequential arm waves whose order rotates across rounds. Every comparison is within one CPU part as read from /proc/cpuinfo; no CPU generation is inferred. Run cost $2.97 (all three arms).

host_variability.method: Every comparison is made within one observed CPU part. Warm (the primary metric): within each round the arms alternate pass by pass (the arm order rotates every pass), so the arms are interleaved within the round, and each (round, request) cell is compared on the same CPU part. Cold and restore waves are sequential arm waves whose position rotates across rounds (a Latin square over 4 rounds): that controls order and round drift but not time-within-round drift. Rows without a CPU part are counted, never compared.

unknown.cgroup: per environment in e15.host.identities; any file the sandbox hides is 'unknown'

hypothesis: E15 Phase 1 (offline, per-node wall time on CPU part 0xd40) attributed ggml_vec_dot_f32 to the six full-attention layers' F32 KQ and KQV matmuls, 10.6% of warm graph time. llama.cpp f74e2fa6a's ggml-cpu.c undefines GGML_USE_LLAMAFILE whenever __ARM_FEATURE_SVE or __ARM_FEATURE_MATMUL_INT8 is set, so the SVE / i8mm CPU variants (armv8.6_1 on 0xd40, armv8.6_2 on 0xd4f) never call llamafile's F32 tinyBLAS sgemm and run KQV through the per-row ggml_vec_dot_f32 loop. Letting those variants use tinyBLAS for F32 x F32 MUL_MAT only (KQ stays on vec_dot because its src1 is not contiguous) makes warm requests faster on those parts; the offline paired probe measured -1.88% per warm request (95% CI -2.10% to -1.64%) with max |delta probability| 0.0101 and 0 choice flips. Parts that load a non-SVE variant (0xd0c, armv8.2_2) already use llamafile and are unchanged.
